platform.note: the original CARE training used 2 Torch threads on macOS; the reference here is regenerated on this platform with 1 thread and deterministic algorithms

inputs.location: artifacts/ (gitignored; CARE-derived data and trained state are not committed to the public repository)
inputs.batches: FrozenPreparation(prepared=care-train-profile-schedule-20261016, dataset=care-numeric-input-20261016, fold=0).batch(step): 8 train-prefix examples, context [8,3,128], actual [8,3,32]; steps 0 and 4095 must equal fold-0-batch-reference.bin byte for byte
inputs.state: the selected fold0 state (step 4096): 59 trainable tensors and the buffers scale_floor, position, time_mask; AdamW step and first/second moments for the mature case

recipe.loss: small_model.training_loss: pinball on normalized quantiles against (actual - context_center) / context_scale, mean over B*C*H*3
recipe.optimizer: AdamW lr 3e-4, betas [0.9, 0.999], eps 1e-8, weight_decay 0.01, decoupled, no amsgrad, foreach/fused off, constant lr (no scheduler)
recipe.clip_coefficient: min(1, max_norm / (global_norm + 1e-6)), global_norm over the 59 per-tensor norms (R0.1 clip_denominator_eps 1e-6)

cases.one_update: selected parameters, fresh AdamW (step 0, zero moments), one update on batch step 0
cases.eight_updates: selected parameters, fresh AdamW, eight updates on batch steps 0..7 in order
cases.mature_import: selected parameters with the saved AdamW step 4096 and moments, one update on batch step 0 (the 4096-step schedule ends at step 4096: FrozenPreparation rejects step >= 4096 and the saved sampler_position is 32768, so the import update uses the first schedule batch, fixed here before any run)
cases.floor_tie: artificial, no CARE data: selected parameters, context = the R1 floor-equal case [1,3,128] (x[c,t] = floor_c for even t, -floor_c for odd t, so the population std equals scale_floor exactly; certified on this platform by the entry check), actual[c,h] = floor_c for even h, -floor_c for odd h; loss and raw/clipped gradients only, no update
cases.resume: Rust only, same backend and threads: continuous eight_updates versus 4 updates, checkpoint write, separate-process restore, 4 updates; byte-exact parameters, moments, counters and outputs (the forward of the next batch) as R0.1 same_backend_resume

starting_state_rationale.choice: cases one_update and eight_updates start from the selected (step 4096) parameters with a fresh AdamW
reasons: R0.1 references pin only the selected state; the initial weights exist only in initial.pt, which no R0.1 reference pins, and converting it would add a new reference
one_update and mature_import then share parameters and batch, so they differ only in the optimizer state (fresh versus step 4096 moments)
measured before fixing: on batch steps 0 and 4095 the excluded fraction at K*eps is 0.28%, far from the 10% stop rule
starting_state_rationale.deviation: the implementation plan says 'saved weight with a fresh optimizer' and 'the same initial weight'; it does not name the initial or the selected weights. Using initial.pt (converted to the neutral format as the plan does for R3) would be the alternative; not chosen for the reasons above

nondifferentiable_boundaries.pinball_tie: R2P L1/L4 (synthetic, passed); real batches had 0 exact ties at steps 0 and 4095
nondifferentiable_boundaries.maximum_std_floor_tie: case floor_tie. context_scale depends only on the input and scale_floor (a buffer), so the subgradient chosen at std == floor cannot change parameter gradients; the case confirms this numerically as R0.1 model.nondifferentiable_boundary requires
nondifferentiable_boundaries.clip_below_one: real batches give global norms of about 0.43 to 0.73 (coefficient 1); the branch that scales gradients (norm > max_norm) is covered by R2P C2/C3/O3, not by real data

compare.loss: every update: normalized_loss for update 1, eight_step_loss for later updates; floor_tie: normalized_loss
compare.gradients: every update and floor_tie, all 59 tensors: raw and clipped under the R0.1 gradient rule, plus global norm and clip coefficient
compare.parameters: after every update: one_step_parameter after update 1 (one_update, mature_import, eight_updates update 1) and eight_step_parameter after updates 2..8 of eight_updates; judged only on elements whose reference clipped |gradient| >= 1e-7 (K=10, eps 1e-8) at every update of that run up to the compared one; mature_import uses only its own update
compare.moments: first_moment and second_moment on all elements after every update
compare.forward: recorded after every update (normalized quantiles of the next batch, or of the last batch after the last update), judged only through the next update's loss

reference.generator: Torch float32 on this platform, run and hashed before any Rust run; saved under artifacts/, only hashes and summaries are committed
reference.independent_check: the same procedure in float64; the float32 reference is kept only if loss and gradients agree with float64 within R0.1 (parameters and moments are recorded, not gated, in this check, because AdamW amplifies rounding where |gradient| is near eps)

run.unit: one invocation of the formal R2 driver, in order: (1) Torch reference and its float64 check, hashed and frozen; (2) Rust one_update, eight_updates, mature_import, floor_tie; (3) Rust resume in separate processes
run.build: cargo build --release --locked before the run, outside the time limits; its duration is recorded
run.harness_failure: a failure that is not a numeric comparison result (crash, I/O, missing file, timeout) may be fixed in the harness only (no fixture, tolerance, recipe or reference change) and the whole driver run again; the frozen reference must reproduce byte for byte and every case that already produced numeric results must reproduce them byte for byte, otherwise stop
run.numeric_failure: any failing element is recorded and stops formal R2; no fixture, tolerance or reference change afterwards
run.float64_check_failure: a numeric failure: formal R2 stops before any Rust run; the reference is not regenerated with other settings
